predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: "Albanian territories taken from Byzantium" by Charles of Anjou, round Durrës, Berat and the coast to Butrint

successors.name: Principality of Albania (Thopia)
successors.text: Durrës, which "Karl Thopia took ... from the Angevins" in 1368

ledger.x: Late February 1272: Charles of Anjou declares the Kingdom of Albania; "Charles signed a treaty with Albanian nobles and Durrës citizens on 21 February 1272".

Page silent on the year: Berat is Byzantine "since 1274" and "later on Butrint" fell to the same Byzantine forces; the page has Nikephoros I's troops capturing Butrint in 1278 and surrendering it to Charles in March 1279, so the 1274-1278 holder was Byzantium (the despotate-of-epirus dossier: 1278 gain from…
March 1279: Nikephoros I of Epirus surrenders Butrint and Sopot to Charles.
December 1280: Angevin forces besiege the castle of Berat; in March 1281 a Byzantine relief army defeats them and captures Hugo de Sully.
March 1281: the siege of Berat fails.
c. 1294: Kaninë, near Vlorë, falls; the page does not name the captor, the Byzantine Empire by the researcher's reading. In August 1294 Charles II passes his Albanian rights to Philip I.
The page says "Corfu and Butrint remained in Angevin hands at least up to 1292" and gives no later date for Butrint; the loss is bridged to 1294, the year Kaninë, the last mainland holdout, falls.
September 1304: Angevin rule is restored at Durrës after the Serbs under Stephen Milutin (who took it in 1296) are expelled.
1368: Karl Thopia takes Durrës from the Angevins (infobox disestablishment).
1368: the Angevin kingdom ends; Louis of Évreux conquers Durrës in 1376 and Thopia regains it in 1383, but the page treats 1368 as the end.

wars.name: Angevin-Byzantine war in Albania
wars.outcome: The Byzantines took Berat (1274) and defeated the Angevin siege of its castle (December 1280 to March 1281); Nikephoros I of Epirus surrendered Butrint and Sopot in March 1279; by 1281 the Angevins were out of the interior.

wars.name: Serbian-Angevin struggle for Durrës
wars.outcome: Stephen Milutin took Durrës in 1296; the Serbs were expelled and Angevin rule was restored in September 1304.

certainty.note: A coastal lordship of cities and castles, with no frontier line on the page; the county shapes are approximate and 1294-1303 has no territory at all.
